question: Two trains are running along parallel tracks towards each other at speeds of 40 km/h and 60 km/h, respectively. If the length of each train is 125 metres, then how much time will they take to cross each other?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/s = 100 × (5/18) = 250/9 m/s.

Total distance covered = 125 + 125 = 250 metres.

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative speed = 250 ÷ (250/9) = 9 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Train 1 = 40 km/h

Speed of Train 2 = 60 km/h

Length of both trains = 125 m each

**Formula Used:**

Time taken to cross = (Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2) ÷ Relative Speed

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

 
 
 
• Train 1 (125m) 
• 40 km/h Train 2 (125m) 
• 60 km/h Total Distance = 125 + 125 = 250 m Relative Speed = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 125 m + 125 m = 250 m

⇒ Relative Speed (moving towards each other) = 40 + 60 = 100 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 100 × (5/18) = 250/9 m/s

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 250 ÷ (250/9)

⇒ Time = (250 × 9) / 250

⇒ Time = 9 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 9 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion Rule

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

When two bodies travel in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Total Distance in Crossing

When a train crosses another train, bridge, or platform, the total distance covered is always the sum of the lengths of both objects (L₁ + L₂).
